- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then decline too sharply, missing sustained upward momentum.
- Model underestimates late-period price spikes (last 5–10 days) — often fails to capture the full magnitude of the trend reversal or breakout.
- Forecasts show a tendency to “overshoot” after sharp price increases, then correct too quickly — suggesting poor lag adjustment.
- Mean reversion is overemphasized — model assumes prices will return to prior levels too soon, ignoring persistent momentum.
- Model fails to account for cumulative momentum — especially when prices are rising steadily over 10+ days.
- Forecasts are overly sensitive to recent volatility — reacting too strongly to short-term noise rather than long-term trends.
- Model underestimates the impact of policy or market events that occur mid-horizon — leading to delayed or muted corrections.
- Forecasts often underestimate the “tail risk” — missing extreme price movements in the final 3–5 days.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility — underestimating the likelihood of sudden, large price jumps or drops.
